statements.t: We expect continued expansion of our vision and safety systems, including MirrorEye® and adjacent products and advanced technologies, through maturity of our existing products and the introduction of new products to the market, including our surround-view capabilities.

As we continue to invest in these capabilities, we have generated a comprehensive technology roadmap that we expect will both enhance and expand on our existing products and bring new products and technologies to the market.
We expect this will drive growth that significantly outpaces our weighted-average end markets resulting in shareholder value creation.

While we expect these actions will benefit financial performance by offsetting cost pressures, there can be no assurance that our mitigation efforts will fully offset the impact of these cost increases.

Over the long-term, we expect our Electronics’ segment sales to continue to outperform forecasted changes in production volumes due to strong demand for our existing products including our OEM MirrorEye programs in North America and Europe as well as from launches of awarded business.
In addition, over the long-term we expect revenue growth and margin contribution from our off-highway products including the launch of a new off-highway vision product in 2027.

We expect our served market channels to moderately improve throughout 2027 based on current market and economic conditions; however our sales of in-region OEM products will continue to be benefited by the launch of an infotainment product in the second quarter of 2026.
In 2026, we expect D&D spend, net of business realignment to increase driven by spend for quality improvement, product cost optimization, and the development of next generation products.

We continue to evaluate and optimize our engineering footprint to enhance capabilities and capacity for the most efficient return on our engineering spend including increasing the utilization of our Stoneridge Brazil engineering function and dedicated engineering partners in India to support Electronics segment projects.

While we expect continued material inflation and supply chain challenges associated with memory and other electronic component pricing and availability to persist into 2027, we continue to focus on operating performance and enterprise-wide cost reduction.
We remain focused on improving cash generation and the reduction of debt through efficient operating performance, structural cost savings and targeted actions to reduce our inventory levels.
However, we anticipate working capital investment in the fourth quarter of 2026 related to the mid-2027 launch of a new off-highway vision product.
The Company’s $10.0 million investment in the Autotech Fund II will be contributed over the expected ten-year life of the fund.
The Company expects to refinance its Credit Facility.
While there can be no assurance that the Company will refinance the current Credit Facility, the Company believes that it is probable the Credit Facility will be refinanced prior to its maturity.

The Company has not experienced a violation that would limit the its ability to borrow under the Credit Facility, as amended, and does not expect the covenants under it to restrict its financing flexibility.
The Company expects to make additional repayments on the Credit Facility when cash exceeds the amount needed for operations and to remain in compliance with all covenants.
In addition, on December 31, 2026, the borrowing capacity on our Credit Facility will decrease to the lesser of $157.5 million or the then current Credit Facility commitment.

The principal sources of liquidity available for our future cash requirements are expected to be (i) cash flows from operations, (ii) cash and cash equivalents on-hand and (iii) borrowings from our Credit Facility .

We expect to fund payment of the PM sensor arbitration award from cash on-hand, including cash held outside the United States, and intend to hold discussions with the former customer regarding the timing of payment.
Payment of the award will reduce our available liquidity and, depending on its timing and amount, could reduce headroom under the financial covenants in the Credit Facility in future periods.
We expect to refinance our Credit Facility prior to its July 1, 2027 termination date.

Based on our current financial position and our refinancing plans, we believe we will have sufficient liquidity to meet our obligations over the next twelve months; however, there can be no assurance that the refinancing will be completed on acceptable terms or at all.

Based on year-to-date results and current expectations for the fourth quarter, the Company is revising its 2026 guidance ranges.

“Given strengthening demand across the European and North American commercial vehicle markets, which is anticipated to carry into 2027, year-to-date outperformance in our Brazilian business, and the demonstrated success of our innovative safety and efficiency enhancing technologies, we now expect 2026 adjusted revenue to exceed our prior expectations.

That said, given the proactive measures we have undertaken to resolve several legacy warranty and inventory-related matters that were not envisioned in our original guidance and uncertainty created by ongoing inflationary cost pressures, in particular for semiconductors, and unfavorable currency movements, we now anticipate that full year adjusted EBITDA will come in at the bottom end of our prior expectations.”
